recipes.name: Methi thepla
instructions: Pick and wash the fresh fenugreek leaves thoroughly, then chop them very finely.
Pound or crush the green chilli into a completely smooth paste using a mortar and pestle.
In a large mixing bowl, combine the whole wheat flour, finely chopped fenugreek leaves, and green chilli paste.
Mix the ingredients together dry with your fingers to evenly distribute the leaves throughout the flour.
Gradually sprinkle small amounts of water and knead firmly into a smooth, soft, and pliable dough.
Divide the kneaded dough into four equal parts and roll each portion into a smooth, round ball.
Roll each ball out very thinly into a uniform circular flatbread using dry flour for dusting.
Place the thin thepla on a smoking hot tawa and cook both sides on medium flame for about one minute until golden spots appear.

recipes.name: Kanda poha maharashtrian
instructions: Place the flattened rice into a colander, wash it gently under running tap water, drain completely, and leave to soften.
Finely chop the raw onion, green chilli, and fresh coriander leaves.
Heat a dry non-stick frying pan over medium-low heat.
Add the chopped onions and fresh curry leaves to the pan and dry-sauté until the onions turn translucent and soft.
Add the chopped green chillies to the pan and cook for one additional minute to infuse the flavor.
Gently fluff the damp, softened flattened rice with your fingers to ensure there are no large clumps.
Add the flattened rice into the pan with the onions and toss carefully from the bottom to prevent breaking the flakes.
Cover the pan with a tight lid, allow it to steam on low heat for three minutes, then turn off flame and garnish with coriander.

recipes.name: Batata poha
instructions: Rinse the flattened rice in a sieve under running water, drain out all excess water, and set aside to puff up.
Peel the raw potato and cut it into very small, uniform cubes to ensure quick and even cooking.
Finely chop the onion and the fresh green chilli.
In a heavy-bottomed pan, add the small potato cubes, cover with a lid, and cook on low heat until they are fork-tender.
Add the chopped onion and fresh curry leaves to the pan with the cooked potatoes and sauté until translucent.
Stir in the chopped green chillies and cook for one minute until fragrant.
Transfer the softened flattened rice into the pan and fold it gently with the vegetable mixture.
Cover the pan with its lid and let it cook on the lowest heat setting for three minutes to steam through thoroughly.

recipes.name: Suji dhokla
instructions: In a deep bowl, combine the semolina with an equal amount of water and stir into a smooth batter.
Add the finely crushed green chilli paste to the semolina batter and mix thoroughly.
Allow the semolina batter to rest covered for ten minutes so the grains absorb water and expand properly.
Set up a steamer with water and bring it to a boil over medium-high heat.
Give the rested batter a final vigorous stir, ensuring it has a thick yet pourable consistency.
Pour the prepared batter immediately into a lightly greased shallow steel steaming plate or tin.
Place the plate inside the preheated steamer, cover securely, and steam on high heat for fifteen minutes.
Remove the plate, allow it to cool slightly, slice into squares, and garnish with dry-toasted curry leaves.

recipes.name: Methi paratha west style
instructions: Clean the fenugreek leaves carefully, wash them in plenty of water to remove grit, and chop fine.
Finely chop the green chilli into tiny pieces.
In a large pan or bowl, blend the whole wheat flour, chopped fenugreek leaves, and green chilli.
Rub the greens completely into the dry flour using your palms until well incorporated.
Slowly pour in water step-by-step and knead the mixture into a firm, smooth dough.
Divide the kneaded dough into two equal-sized rounds and roll them out into smooth circular shapes.
Using a rolling pin on a flat surface, roll each ball out into an even round flatbread.
Cook the paratha on a preheated tawa over medium-high heat, turning once, until both sides are well browned.
